text:
sophie chen: FYI rolling up a canary for kaito11b int4. seeing two things: slowstart (first 10-20 tokens very slow) and intermittent OOMs on warm starts. also a small perf regression vs fp16 on the chat benchmarks. anyone seen this pattern before?
rami singh: saw similar on another int4 bringup — memory fragmentation + aggressive prefetch seemed to spike allocations during kv warmup.
aj: got logs? stack traces?
sophie chen: pasted a minimal log snippet below (truncated):
```
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] serve: new request id=abc123 seq=0 model=kaito11b-int4
[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] runtime: allocate kv_cache 256MB -> success
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] runtime: prefetch slots=6 took=340ms
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] runtime: allocate scratch 1.2GB failed: cudaOutOfMemory
[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] runtime: fallback eviction triggered, retry
[2026-03-20T14:02:13Z] runtime: generation slow (token 1-5) latency=520ms/token
```
leila ortiz: that `prefetch slots=6` + scratch alloc failure smells like aggressive slot reservation + quantized kernels allocating unexpected workspace. what are default `max_new_tokens` and `batch_size` for the canary?
sophie chen: defaults: `max_new_tokens=256`, `batch_size=8` (per-GPU continuous batching).
leila ortiz: try 1) lower `batch_size` to 4 for canary 2) reduce `max_new_tokens` to 128 as temporary default 3) set `prefetch_slots=2` and `kv_evict_threshold=0.65` in the config. small experiment script: `./run_canary.sh --batch 4 --max_new 128 --prefetch 2`.
rami singh: also tune the allocator: enable `cuda_cushion=0.06` and `fragmentation_defrag_interval=30s` for the canary pool, that helped on nova27b.
aj: curious about the quality regression vs fp16 — is it decoding artifacts or logits shift? can you share eval diff?
sophie chen: quick numbers from our eval harness (QA+Chatty): int4 BLEU-ish delta ~ -0.7, F1 down ~ -1.1. most failures are subtle stop-token truncation and occasional repetition. sample: prompt "Summarize..." produced trimmed tails.
leila ortiz: that can be quant noise at high token lengths. try enabling `quant-stochastic-rounding=true` for the transformer kernels or fallback the final linear to fp16 (`hetero-fp-final=true`). also cap `max_new_tokens` by route for long-form tasks.
infra-bot: deploy candidate `kaito11b-int4-v2` rolled to canary (2 GPUs). config: `{batch_size:4,max_new_tokens:128,prefetch_slots:2,cuda_cushion:0.06}`. monitoring: heatmaps enabled.
aj: good. one more thought: if slowstart only affects first requests after idle, we might be hitting cold KV cache + first-token kernel compilation/path selection. enable warmstart with `prewarm=true --warmup_prompts 5` in the canary runner to populate KV and kernels.
rami singh: agree — prefilling KV and running a short load of short prompts reduces the 1st-token tail latency 3x. also set `kernel-cache=on` on the nodes.
sophie chen: running the patched canary now. will report back numbers in ~30m. thanks all :thumbsup:
leila ortiz: if OOMs persist after these tweaks, we'll try a live fallback policy: accept int4 but fallback to fp16 for requests where `total_request_bytes > 1GB` (heuristic) and log rates.
sophie chen: noted. will add fallback rule and update the rollout plan.
infra-bot: alert: canary `kaito11b-int4-v2` memory pressure reduced by 18% in first 20m after config change. ongoing metrics at https://dash.internal/redwood/canaries/kaito11b-int4-v2
sophie chen: nice. closing loop after full 4h smoke.
